Internal: the built-in report style

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_style_report.Rd

The second built-in (ruling R58, Session 408; built Session 409): a SHORT style based on apa, which stays the complete root of every based.on chain. It holds only the values the report style manuals share where apa's differ – the UK Government Analysis Function, the Australian Government Style Manual, the UN Editorial Manual, and the US agencies' forms, which differ from it by a setting or two (the Table Layer Reference, 8.8): Arial 10, the caption 10 and the note 9, "Table 1:" with the title on one line, a light grey bold header, apa's three rules, no banding, the zero before the point (build 1's lean, Session 409: most of the guidance writes it – NIH, the GPO manual, CDC's Emerging Infectious Diseases, the Australian and UK manuals – and NCES's table guidelines alone drop it on a statistic that cannot exceed 1; Jeff: "Okay to keep your lean in this"), an upright "Note:", each variable's label row bold. The new looks (caption.fill, heading.fill) stay off, so a brand look is only ever turned on, in a user's own short file based on this one.

Usage

.jst_style_report
